name: Cottonwood Ridge Traverse
region: Wasatch Range, between Big and Little Cottonwood Canyons

legs.route: Broads Fork trail, then the north ridge of the Twins

legs.connect: Descend the south ridge from the Twins and scramble sharp, exposed ridge to Sunrise.
Follow the ridge east; a couloir here offers the usual bail-out.
Continue along the exposed crest over smaller teeth to the final steep rock.
Optional extension along the crest after Monte Cristo.

how: A sharp ridge line with fourth-class scrambling and some low fifth-class moves. The stretch from the Twins to Sunrise is the hardest by one account, and Monte Cristo's west face is the final crux. Bail-outs exist at the saddle between Sunrise and Dromedary, which is why many do only the first three peaks. A helmet and some rope for downclimbs are sensible.
descent: The full line ends on the far side of the divide, down a pole line or trail toward a ski-area base; the shorter version drops east into a lake basin and a trail back. Neither retraces the ridge.
logistics: Needs a car shuttle or ride between the two canyons for the full line. Start before dawn for the long version. Best in dry months; spring snow routes use a gully approach.
notes: Variants differ: one report starts at a different trailhead, finishes at Alta and omits the Twins. The Triple Traverse (Twins, Sunrise, Dromedary) is a shorter subset. Superior is optional. SummitPost route page returned 403. Class from reports: 4th class, brief 5th.

name: Bullion Divide

legs.route: Hiking trail from the Alta side

legs.connect: Walk the ridge to the next summit.
Follow the road along the ridge; the tram summit is here.

legs.route: Northeast ridge, including the western true summit
legs.connect: Leave the ski area and scramble the ridge west.
Continue along the ridge to a gentle summit.
Climb the next ridge with some third-class steps.

legs.route: Traverse from Red Baldy, then the northwest ridge
legs.connect: Cross the narrow crest, the crux, to the last summit.

how: A ridge walk and scramble of about eleven miles that links the high points of the divide above the canyon. Fourth-class scrambling and loose rock in places, with the crossing from Red Baldy to White Baldy being the hardest. Parties go in both directions, and some begin at the top of the tram to shorten the first part. A helmet is wise, and in winter and spring an ice axe and crampons.
descent: Descend White Baldy's northwest ridge, then a hiking trail to the canyon. An optional extension adds the east ridge of the Pfeifferhorn and a different descent.
logistics: Needs a car shuttle between the two ends of the canyon, or a ride. Some versions add extra summits such as Devil's Castle. Weather can shorten the route; escape lines drop to the ski area.
notes: Direction conflicts: Mountain Project lists east to west; the club report went west to east. Peak lists differ slightly (club includes Devil's Castle and a sub-peak). Only two pages read in full.
